A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reWordBench study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations under 28 transformations, regularized-model training experiments, and downstream best-of-n and RAFT results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds GPT-4o benchmark results and downstream evaluations using a Qwen judge.

M1.justification: The proposed paraphrase-based reward consistency objective in Equation 3 and the training and alignment procedures remain unchanged. Newly mentioned preliminary tests of alternative losses do not change the adopted method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RewardBench categories, 28 transformation scenarios, HelpSteer2 training data, and UltraFeedback alignment data. Adding evaluated models and another judge does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o to the ten reward models evaluated in the benchmark comparison, with results in Figure 2 and Table 11. The standard, data-augmentation, and regularized-model comparison in Table 5 is retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces prompted preference selection for GPT-4o and adds Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as a second judge of downstream outputs. Existing splits, training budgets, best-of-64 settings, and response-length controls remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and Appendix D extend evaluator-sensitivity checks to Qwen, including the existing length-matched analysis. Section 5 also newly reports that alternative losses such as Huang et al. (2023) underperformed in preliminary experiments. The regularization-strength analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these comparisons. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o results, including accuracy decreasing from 0.99 to 0.45 under Append Other Code in Table 11, and Qwen evaluations in Figure 4. Appendix D adds Qwen length-controlled win rates of 50%, 54%, and 47%. Shared Table 5 results and prior Llama-judge results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The reward-model definitions, ranking-invariance formulation, and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. The ranking-robustness paragraph is relocated without revising its mathematics; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: documenting reward-model brittleness with reWordBench and improving robustness and downstream alignment through paraphrase regularization. Added evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains that the optimal regularization coefficient depends on the transformation and identifies training on additional transformations as future work. It also interprets cross-judge agreement as evidence of robustness, although the new length-controlled Qwen results provide mixed support and the concluding interpretation remains insufficiently qualified.

D1.justification: Appendix A identifies the added GPT-4o snapshot as gpt-4o-2024-11-20, and Appendix C specifies reuse of the evaluation prompt for it. Section 5.3 identifies the added Qwen judge. Appendix G's training and implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references connecting paraphrase training to Maini et al. and Yang et al., expands discussion of robustness benchmarks and consistency regularization, and attributes Figure 1's example to Zeng et al. The existing novelty claim and overall research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions, explanatory additions, and footnote changes, including shorter transformation descriptions and revised discussion of model rankings. The main section sequence and appendix organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains GPT-4o bars, Figure 4 gains judge labels and Qwen rows, and Table 11 gains a GPT-4o column. Table 5 and Figure 3 move with the surrounding text, and Figure 1's caption gains attribution. The overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: The GPT-4o comparison broadens the tested model set, while the independent Qwen judge strengthens validation of downstream benefits in Figure 4. These provide a limited overall improvement. However, Appendix D's new 50%/54%/47% length-controlled win rates do not uniformly support superiority, and v2 retains an overly broad positive interpretation of that analysis.
